sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Togo.
Togo is a small, colorful, and friendly country
in West Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Togo?
Togo is in West Africa.
It is next to Ghana, Benin, and Burkina Faso.
To the south, it touches the Atlantic Ocean.
Togo has beaches, hills, and forests.
What is the capital city of Togo?
The capital city is Lome.
Lome is on the coast by the sea.
It has markets, museums, offices, and beaches.
It is the largest city in Togo.
Other towns include Cara in the north.
Socode in the center.
Attack Palme near the mountains.
How many people live in Togo?
About 8.5 million people live in Togo.
Some live in cities, but many live in villages
and rural areas.
Togo is a multicultural country with many ethnic groups.
What language do people speak in Togo?
The official language is French.
People also speak local languages like in the south,
Cabilla in the north, Mina, Tem, and others.
Many people speak two or three languages in daily life.
What is the weather like in Togo?
Togo has a tropical climate.
It is hot and humid near the coast.
It is drier in the north.
There are two rainy seasons and two dry seasons.
Most of the year is warm with lots of sun.
What does Togo look like?
Togo has long beaches on the coast,
green hills in the center,
forests and savannas, mountains and rivers in the north.
It is a narrow country but full of natural beauty.
What animals live in Togo?
In Togo you can see monkeys, antelopes and bats,
snakes, lizards, and frogs.
Cows, goats, and chickens on farms,
birds, fish, and insects.
Togo has national parks to protect wildlife.
What do people eat in Togo?
Togolese food is simple, flavorful, and filling.
People eat maize, cassava, and millet,
rice, yams, and plantains,
fish, chicken, and goat,
peanuts, tomatoes, and spices.
Popular dishes, fufu, soft dough made from cassava or yams.
Putt, thick porridge made from maize flour,
rizz sauce, arachied, rice with peanut sauce.
Acpan, fermented maize with sugar,
steamed corn cakes.
What do people drink in Togo?
People drink water and fruit juice,
tea and coffee,
beesap, hibiscus flour drink,
ginger juice.
Adults may drink palm wine or local beer.
In hot weather, people drink a lot of water to stay cool.
What is life like in Togo?
Life in Togo is often traditional,
busy, and community-based.
People enjoy spending time with family,
working in markets or on farms,
going to church or mosque,
dancing, drumming, and storytelling,
helping neighbors and celebrating together.
Children often play football or run barefoot outside.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, April 27,
Edal Feeder and Edal Adha,
Christmas and New Year,
traditional festivals with music,
masks, and dances.
Yam Festival, a harvest celebration in many villages,
people wear bright clothes,
and music is a big part of every event.
Some fun facts about Togo.
Togo is one of the smallest countries in Africa.
The Togalese flag is green,
yellow, and red with a white star.
People often carry things on their heads.
Football is the most popular sport.
Togo means behind the river in the U-language.
Now you know many things about Togo.
You know where it is,
what people eat,
and how they live.
You learned about the beaches,
music, and food.
Well done.
I am Emili.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in you, wasa.
